# #307 — openbrain-memory: spool replay has no production dispatcher — spooled durable records never drain

State: CLOSED
Author: rodaddy
Labels: none

Updated: 2026-07-21T04:03:48Z

## Problem

`Spool.replay()` and `replay_records()` (python/openbrain-memory/src/openbrain_memory/spool.py) are public API with **only test callers**. Nothing in the runtime, adapter, or any CLI ever replays the spool in production. A record that gets spooled (receipt `status:"spooled"`, `durable:true`) is durable forever but never delivered.

Observed live during the 0.1.9 provider rollout: core01 accumulated 5 redacted diagnostic records in `~/.local/state/openbrain-memory/claude-spool.jsonl` (written while token scope-proof was failing). After the token fix, subsequent captures return `saved` — but the spooled records just sit there. Even a successful `session-start` recall with a valid token does not drain them.

## Why it matters

The `spooled` receipt contract says durable — the implicit promise is eventual delivery. Without any production replay path, "durable" actually means "parked in a file nobody reads". This also blocks the #304 follow-up (replaying pre-fix spools) and interacts with the #300 saturation semantics: a spool that never drains only ever fills.

## Proposed shape

- A `replay` entry point on the package CLI (the runtime request envelope or a subcommand) that builds a dispatcher over the authenticated client and calls `Spool.replay()`, honoring idempotency keys and group units.
- Adapter wiring: after a successful direct operation (or on session-start), opportunistically replay when `pending_count > 0`, bounded and fail-quiet.
- Replay of records written by pre-redaction versions should honor the #304 caveat (they may contain raw payloads; replaying transmits them — that is delivery, not disclosure, but worth stating).

## Refs

- #304 (redact-before-persist; pre-fix spool replay follow-up)
- #300 (saturation/backpressure semantics — `SpoolFullError`)
